地点与对象
日本据世界卫生组织估计,超过800,000人携带慢性乙型肝炎。
事件
葛兰素史克 (GSK) 的 慢性乙型肝炎 药物贝匹罗韦森(品牌为 Hibsago)已获得全球首个批准,商品名为 功能性治愈 慢性乙型肝炎。成功的后期试验证实了这一点,该试验表明该药物可以帮助五分之一的患者达到 功能性治愈。
规模、影响与风险
The drug is approved as the first and only functional cure for chronic hepatitis B in Japan. It is expected to generate over £2bn in peak annual sales, addressing a significant health issue with a large affected population.
应对、状态与不确定性
该批准已得到确认,FDA 已承诺对 Jemperli 治疗直肠癌进行优先审查。该药物的作用机制被描述为靶向病毒 DNA 复制、降低表面抗原水平和增强 免疫应答。没有提及未解决的信息。

GSK Wins Approval for New Hepatitis B Drug - EMJ

News Brief
GSK has received its first global approval for its chronic hepatitis B drug, bepirovirsen, branded as Hibsago, in Japan. This approval marks the first and only functional cure for chronic hepatitis B in the country, where over 800,000 people are estimated to live with the disease, according to the WHO. The drug was approved following successful late-stage trials that demonstrated its ability to help one in five patients achieve a functional cure. Bepirovirsen works by blocking viral DNA replication, reducing hepatitis B surface antigen levels in the blood, and enhancing immune response for longer-term control of the virus. The company also announced that the FDA will prioritize its review of Jemperli as a potential treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer, with an action date set for February 2027. These regulatory wins come as part of GSK's broader strategy to expand its drug development pipelines in oncology and other therapeutic areas. The approval is a significant milestone in the treatment of chronic hepatitis B, offering an alternative to lifelong antiviral therapy.

GSK predicts the hepatitis B drug could generate over £2bn in peak annual sales. The FDA will prioritise its review of Jemperli as a potential treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer. GSK has received its first global approval for its chronic hepatitis B drug and key support for a potential rectal cancer therapy, it announced on Monday. The British pharmaceutical giant shared that bepirovirsen, to be branded as Hibsago, has been approved as the first and only functional cure for chronic hepatitis B in Japan – where it is estimated over 800,000 people live with the disease, according to the WHO. First functional cure for hepatitis B The approval comes after successful late-stage trials proved the drug to be successful in helping one in five patients reach a functional cure for hepatitis B. Bepirovirsen works by blocking viral DNA replication, lowering hepatitis B surface antigen levels in the blood and boosting the immune response for longer lasting control of the virus, tackling the disease three-fold. As the first approved finite treatment course that can be used as an alternative to lifelong antiviral pills to achieve functional cure, it leads the way for a new wave of next-generation therapies. GSK has predicted that the new drug could bring in over £2bn ($2.73bn) in peak annual sales, bringing it closer to its annual revenue goal of over £40bn by 2031. Cancer therapy review expected The firm also announced that the FDA has committed to carrying out a priority review of another of its drugs, Jemperli (dostarlimab), as a potential treatment for a type of rectal cancer, alongside its existing approvals for specific endometrial cancer subtypes. The FDA has assigned February 2027 as the action date for the rectal cancer review, with the program structure possibly yielding a decision earlier. Jemperli, which is not currently approved anywhere in the world for the treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer, also received Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations by the FDA. These two regulatory wins for the company come just weeks after it launched a £1.9bn ($2.52bn) cost-savings effort to help fund its expanded late-stage study roster and deliver on CEO Luke Miels’ promise for faster drug development. The restructuring is a major step by the company’s boss to reassure investors that GSK can navigate a looming patent deadline for its blockbuster HIV drug, dolutegravir, between 2028 and 2030. HIV is currently the company’s leading specialty therapy area by revenue, but GSK said it now expects to start 25 late-stage studies by the end of 2026 in an effort to continue to expand pipelines in oncology and respiratory, immunology and inflammation. The firm also announced that the FDA has committed to carrying out a priority review of another of its drugs, ⁠Jemperli (dostarlimab), as a potential treatment for a type of rectal cancer, alongside its existing approvals for specific ​endometrial cancer subtypes. The FDA has assigned February ​2027 as the action ⁠date for the rectal cancer review, with the program structure possibly yielding a decision earlier. Jemperli, which is not currently approved anywhere in the world for the treatment of locally advanced rectal cancer, also received ⁠Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations by the FDA. These two regulatory wins for the company come just weeks after it launched a £1.9bn ($2.52bn) cost-savings effort to help fund its expanded late-stage study roster and deliver on CEO Luke Miels’ promise for faster drug development. The restructuring is a major step by the company’s boss to reassure investors that GSK can navigate a looming patent deadline for its blockbuster HIV drug, dolutegravir, between 2028 and 2030. HIV is currently the company’s leading specialty therapy area by revenue, but GSK said it now expects to start 25 late-stage studies by ​the end of 2026 in an effort to continue to expand pipelines in oncology and respiratory, immunology and inflammation. Featured image: MAXSHOT_PL on Adobe Stock. Author: Cecilia Adamou. Close context player
View five news elements
Time
24 Aug 2026 (publication date), 24 Aug 2026 (event date).
Location and population
Japan, estimated over 800,000 people living with chronic hepatitis B, according to the WHO.
Event
GSK has received its first global approval for its chronic hepatitis B drug, bepirovirsen (branded as Hibsago), as a functional cure treatment for chronic hepatitis B. This is confirmed by the successful late-stage trials that showed the drug can help one in five patients reach a functional cure.
Scale, impact and risk
The drug is approved as the first and only functional cure for chronic hepatitis B in Japan. It is expected to generate over £2bn in peak annual sales, addressing a significant health issue with a large affected population.
Response, status and uncertainty
The approval is confirmed, and the FDA has committed to a priority review of Jemperli for rectal cancer. The drug's mechanism is described as targeting viral DNA replication, lowering surface antigen levels, and boosting immune response. No unresolved information is mentioned.

C端截短的乙型肝炎病毒 X转录上调纤溶酶原激活剂抑制剂-1对肝细胞癌发展的影响 - EurekAlert!

The effect of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 transcriptionally upregulated by c-terminal truncated hepatitis B virus X on the development of hepatocellular carcinoma - EurekAlert!
新闻简报该研究于2026年8月25日发表在《中华医学杂志》上,探讨了C端截短的乙型肝炎病毒 X蛋白(Ct-HBx)通过上调纤溶酶原激活物抑制剂-1(PAI-1)促进肝细胞癌(HCC)的作用。这项研究由上海第二军医大学的曹广文及其同事进行,将肝癌细胞系的机制实验与临床 队列研究 分析相结合。它揭示了 Ct-HBx 增强了 PAI-1 启动子和 3’UTR 处的染色质可及性,从而增加了 PAI-1 的表达。PAI-1 中的功能性 SNP(rs2227631-G、rs11178-T、rs1050955-A)与较高的 PAI-1 水平和 HBV-HCC 易感性增加相关。这些 SNP 与 HCC 风险 HBV 突变 相互作用,从而成倍提高风险。血清 PAI-1 水平在 HBV 诱导的肝癌发生过程中升高,并与 HBV-HCC 患者术后不良结局相关。该研究将 PAI-1 确定为 HBV-HCC 的新型预后和预测生物标志物,为 HBV 相关 HCC 发展的表观遗传机制提供了新的见解。

地点与对象
该研究涉及肝癌细胞系和大规模临床队列研究,人群为感染HBV的个体。该研究是在中国进行的,作者隶属于上海第二军医大学。
事件
该研究探讨了 C 端截短的 HBV X 蛋白 (Ct-HBx) 上调纤溶酶原激活剂抑制剂-1 (PAI-1) 转录的机制及其在 HBV 相关肝细胞癌 (HCC) 发展中的作用。研究结果由作者报告并发表在《中华医学杂志》上。
规模、影响与风险
该研究确定了 PAI-1 中的三个功能性 SNP(rs2227631-G、rs11178-T、rs1050955-A),这些 SNP 会增加其表达和 HBV-HCC 易感性。这些 SNP 与 HCC 风险 HBV 突变 相互作用,成倍提高 HBV-HCC 风险。血清 PAI-1 水平在 HBV 诱导的肝癌发生过程中升高,并且与 HBV-HCC 患者术后预后不良相关。
应对、状态与不确定性
该研究是一份同行评审出版物,其研究结果基于机械实验和临床 队列研究 分析。该研究提供了对 HBV-HCC 发展的表观遗传途径的见解,并将 PAI-1 确定为潜在的生物标志物。证据来自信誉良好的来源,结果得到实验和临床数据的支持。
B routine priorityPublic-health news

The effect of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 transcriptionally upregulated by c-terminal truncated hepatitis B virus X on the development of hepatocellular carcinoma - EurekAlert!

News Brief
This study, published on August 25, 2026, in the Chinese Medical Journal, explores the role of the C-terminal truncated hepatitis B virus X protein (Ct-HBx) in promoting hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) through the upregulation of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1). The research, conducted by Guangwen Cao and colleagues at the Second Military Medical University in Shanghai, combines mechanistic experiments in hepatoma cell lines with clinical cohort analyses. It reveals that Ct-HBx enhances chromatin accessibility at the PAI-1 promoter and 3’UTR, increasing PAI-1 expression. Functional SNPs in PAI-1 (rs2227631-G, rs11178-T, rs1050955-A) are associated with higher PAI-1 levels and increased HBV-HCC susceptibility. These SNPs interact with HCC-risk HBV mutations to elevate the risk multiplicatively. Serum PAI-1 levels rise during HBV-induced hepatocarcinogenesis and are linked to poor postoperative outcomes in HBV-HCC patients. The study identifies PAI-1 as a novel prognostic and predictive biomarker for HBV-HCC, offering new insights into the epigenetic mechanisms of HBV-related HCC development.
Original source text (English)
Advanced Search Home News Releases Multimedia Meetings Login Register News Release 25-Aug-2026 The effect of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 transcriptionally upregulated by c-terminal truncated hepatitis B virus X on the development of hepatocellular carcinoma Ct-HBx upregulates PAI-1 via chromatin opening; regulatory polymorphisms and HBV mutations promote hepatocarcinogenesis and affect survival Peer-Reviewed Publication Chinese Medical Journals Publishing House Co., Ltd. Facebook X LinkedIn WeChat Bluesky Message WhatsApp Email image: Ct-HBx is more potent than WT-HBx in upregulating histone acetyltransferases (GCN5, KAT6A) and chromatin remodeling factors (BAF155, ATRX), enhancing chromatin accessibility of the -1kb promoter and the 3’UTR of PAI-1 to promote PAI-1 expression. PAI-1 functional SNPs (rs2227631-G, rs11178-T, rs1050955-A) increase its expression and interact with HCC-risk HBV mutations to synergistically elevate HBV-HCC susceptibility. Serum PAI-1 levels gradually rise during HBV-induced hepatocarcinogenesis. Higher expression of PAI-1 predict poor prognosis in HBV-HCC, identifying PAI-1 as a novel prognostic and predictive biomarker for HBV-HCC. view more Credit: Chinese Medical Journal The development of hepatitis B virus-related hepatocellular carcinoma (HBV-HCC) involves complex interactions between viral factors and host genetics. A hallmark event in HBV-HCC progression is the integration of the HBV gene into the hepatocyte genome. This integration frequently results in truncation of the HBV X (HBx) gene, yielding C-terminal carboxy-truncated HBx (Ct-HBx), which exhibits stronger oncogenic potential than its wild-type counterpart. Previous work identified plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1) as a key effector of Ct-HBx, but the underlying mechanisms and clinical implications remained unclear. To address this, we investigated the mechanisms by which the genetic predisposition and expression of PAI-1 influence Ct-HBx-induced hepatocarcinogenesis and to identify novel predictive and prognostic biomarkers for HBV-HCC. The comprehensive study combined mechanistic experiments in hepatoma cell lines with large-scale clinical cohort analyses. ATAC-seq revealed that Ct-HBx more potently upregulates histone acetyltransferases (GCN5, KAT6A) and chromatin remodelers (BAF155, ATRX) than wild-type HBx (WT-HBx). This enhances chromatin accessibility of the -1kb promoter and the 3’UTR of PAI-1, increasing its expression. In addition, our co-transfection experiment demonstrated that Ct-HBx and WT-HBx almost equally upregulated the expression of the -1kb promoter- or the 3’UTR-regulatory gene, regardless of their functional polymorphic genotypes. Thus, Ct-HBx specifically upregulates the expression of PAI-1 in two ways: (i) Ct-HBx is more potent than WT-HBx in opening chromatin at regulatory regions by upregulating the expression of histone acetyltransferases and chromatin remodeling factors; and (ii) it trans-activates the regulatory regions to express PAI-1, with an almost equal trans-activation capacity to that of WT-HBx. The genetic polymorphic genotypes in the promoter region (rs2227631-G) and in the 3’UTR region (rs11178-T and rs1050955-A) increased the risk of HBV-HCC. These three genetic polymorphic genotypes increased the transcription and mRNA stability of PAI-1, thus increasing the expression of PAI-1, respectively. Previous studies did not investigate the biological functions of SNPs. Here, we demonstrated, for the first time, that the functional polymorphic genotypes rs2227631-GG and rs11178-TT of PAI-1 increased the risk of HBV-HCC by promoting the expression of PAI-1 and participating in the immunoselection of HBV mutations. Specifically, the polymorphic genotypes predisposing to higher PAI-1 expression were often associated with higher frequencies of HCC-risk HBV mutations. Importantly, the interaction between these genotypes and HCC-risk HBV mutations multiplicatively elevated HBV-HCC risk. Longitudinal monitoring in a nested cohort revealed that serum concentration of PAI-1 increased consecutively in HBV-infected subjects who eventually developed HCC but not in those without HCC; furthermore, PAI-1 levels increased significantly after HCC occurred. Furthermore, in a postoperative cohort study, rs2227631-GG at the PAI-1 promoter was associated with increased expression of PAI-1 in tumors; the same was true for rs11178-TT at the 3’UTR. rs2227631-GG and rs11178-TT were independent risk factors for poor postoperative prognosis in patients with HBV-HCC. In addition, higher PAI-1 expression in tumors significantly predicts a poorer prognosis in patients with HBV-positive HCC, but not in HBV-negative HCC. In conclusion, this study elucidates a novel epigenetic pathway wherein Ct-HBx promotes HBV-HCC by opening chromatin to upregulate PAI-1. PAI-1 levels and its functional genotypes serve as promising biomarkers for predicting HCC risk and postoperative prognosis. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to investigate the mechanisms by which Ct-HBx promotes the expression of PAI-1 and to characterize the effects of genetic predispositions and expression of PAI-1 and its interactions with HBV mutations on the development of HBV-HCC, indicating that PAI-1 might be a novel prognostic and predictive biomarker for HBV-HCC. Florida Moves to Drop Hepatitis B, Chickenpox, Hib and Pneumococcal Shots from Public and Private School Rules - Medical Daily
新闻简报佛罗里达州卫生部提议从学前班至十二年级学生的入学要求中删除四种 疫苗——乙型肝炎、水痘(水痘)、b 型流感嗜血杆菌 (Hib) 和肺炎球菌结合物。这项政策变更于 2026 年 8 月 26 日宣布,允许家长和大学生选择不将其免疫记录纳入佛罗里达州 SHOTS 州 疫苗 登记处。该提案正在接受审查,自 2026 年 8 月 20 日起将有为期 21 天的公众评议期。该规则可在卫生局局长批准后通过,并在向国务院备案后生效。证据中没有报告具体的病例数、死亡人数或风险水平。该决定是基于州通过机构规则而不是法规制定免疫要求的权力,并且不需要立法批准。

Florida Moves to Drop Hepatitis B, Chickenpox, Hib and Pneumococcal Shots from Public and Private School Rules - Medical Daily

News Brief
The Florida Department of Health has proposed removing four vaccines—Hepatitis B, chickenpox (varicella), Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib), and pneumococcal conjugate—from school entry requirements for students in prekindergarten through twelfth grade. This policy change, announced on August 26, 2026, allows parents and college students to opt out of having their immunization records included in the state vaccine registry, Florida SHOTS. The proposal is under review, with a 21-day public comment period starting August 20, 2026. The rule can be adopted with the Surgeon General's approval and will take effect once filed with the Department of State. No specific case counts, death counts, or risk levels are reported in the evidence. The decision is based on the state's authority to set immunization requirements via agency rule, not statute, and does not require legislative approval.

Conditions Florida Moves to Drop Hepatitis B, Chickenpox, Hib and Pneumococcal Shots from Public and Private School Rules Published Aug 26, 2026 6:20 AM EDT By Cole Mercer YURIY DYACHYSHYN | AFP via Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pocket The Florida Department of Health has formally proposed a rule to remove four vaccines from the state's school entry requirements, naming hepatitis B, varicella, Haemophilus influenzae type b, and pneumococcal conjugate as immunizations that would no longer be required for attendance in public and private schools from prekindergarten through twelfth grade. Surgeon General Dr. Joseph Ladapo approved the rule on August 20, opening a 21-day window for public comment before final approval, according to Health News Florida. Under state law, the department can adopt the rule with the Surgeon General's approval, and it takes effect once filed with the Department of State. Because the four requirements were set by agency rule rather than statute, the department can remove them without legislative approval. The department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. For Florida families, the change is narrower than much of the national coverage suggests, and the distinction is the single most useful thing a parent can understand this week. Seven other required immunizations are written into Florida statute rather than agency rule, and the health department cannot touch them. The Four Vaccines Named in the Rule, and the Ones That Stay The four vaccines in the proposal protect against distinct and serious conditions. Hepatitis B is a liver infection that can become chronic. Varicella is chickenpox. Hib and pneumococcal conjugate vaccines both protect against bacterial infections that can cause meningitis, and the pneumococcal vaccine also protects against pneumonia. Requirements for measles, mumps, rubella, polio, diphtheria, whooping cough and tetanus are set in state law and remain in place unless the Legislature acts, as NBC News has reported. No legislator filed a bill to remove them in any of this year's legislative sessions, even though the push to end all mandates has been backed by Governor Ron DeSantis. Attempts to pass a medical freedom bill, which would have expanded exemptions and required doctors to offer an alternative schedule, cleared the state Senate and failed in the House. The proposed rule does two additional things that have drawn less attention. It expands religious exemptions to cover moral and ethical beliefs, a materially broader standard than the current religious tenets language. It also allows parents and college students to opt out of having their records included in the state vaccine registry, known as Florida SHOTS, the database that schools and clinicians use to verify immunization status. Twenty-One Days of Comment Stand Between the Rule and Adoption The rule is proposed, not adopted. That timing detail matters for any parent trying to decide whether anything changes before the current school year ends. Nothing changes during the comment window. Florida's existing requirements remain enforceable, and schools continue to collect the state immunization certification form, DH 680. Only after the comment period closes and the rule is filed with the Department of State does it take effect. Parents who have already submitted records for this school year do not need to resubmit anything, and children currently enrolled are not affected while the rule is pending. The department has held a public session on the proposal before, and it was contentious. At a workshop in Panama City Beach in December, pediatricians and infectious disease specialists urged the department to reconsider while vaccine critics supported the plan, as CBS News Miami reported. Physicians at that session described treating children for Hib and for meningitis, conditions these vaccines help prevent. Parents in Miami, Tampa and Orlando Face a Records Question First The immediate household task in Florida is administrative rather than medical, and it is worth doing during the comment window rather than after. Parents should confirm what is actually documented on their child's immunization record, because a requirement being lifted does not remove a vaccine from the recommended childhood schedule. Pediatricians will continue to recommend all four. What changes is whether a school can require documentation before enrollment. The registry opt-out provision deserves particular attention from families who move, change pediatricians, or use walk-in clinics. If a child's records are not in the state database, the burden of proving immunization status shifts entirely to the parent, and reconstructing a vaccine history years later is difficult. Families who want their records retained should understand that opting out is a choice, not the default. Cost is not the barrier it might appear to be. The federal Vaccines for Children program covers the recommended childhood schedule at no cost for eligible children, including those who are uninsured or on Medicaid, through participating pediatricians and county health departments. Removing a school requirement does not remove that coverage. Pediatricians Point to Diseases Most Parents Have Never Seen The clinical objection from physicians has been consistent, and it centers on how invisible these four diseases have become. American Academy of Pediatrics president Dr. Susan Kressly said in a statement responding to the state's broader push that schools are an important part of the community children depend on, and that "close contact makes it easy for contagious diseases to spread quickly." Dr. Eehab Kenawy, a Panama City pediatrician, told the department at the earlier session that religious exemptions already give families a way to decline, and that the state does not need to signal that vaccines are unimportant to preserve that choice. "You're not forced," he said. The backdrop is a measurable national decline. Kindergarten exemptions from at least one vaccine reached a record 4.2 percent nationally, and coverage fell for every routinely reported childhood vaccine, according to new CDC figures reported by MedicalDaily. What remains genuinely unknown is the effect. No one can yet measure how many Florida families would skip these four vaccines if the requirement were to disappear, because the rule has not taken effect and Florida already permits religious exemptions. The department has not published a projected impact on coverage. The Legislature does not reconvene until its next session, and no bill targeting the statutory vaccines has been filed. MedicalDaily will report the outcome of the comment period and the filing date. Hepatitis B, varicella, Haemophilus influenzae type b, and pneumococcal conjugate would be removed from school entry requirements for prekindergarten through twelfth grade at public and private schools. Which requirements stay in place? Measles, mumps, rubella, polio, diphtheria, whooping cough, and tetanus remain required. Those are set in Florida statute and can only be changed by the Legislature. Has the rule taken effect? No. It was approved by the Surgeon General and is now in a 21-day public comment period. It takes effect only after it is filed with the Department of State. Does this mean the four vaccines are no longer recommended? No. They remain part of the recommended childhood immunization schedule, and pediatricians will continue to recommend them. The rule addresses school documentation requirements, not medical guidance. What else does the rule change? It expands religious exemptions to include moral and ethical beliefs and allows parents and college students to opt out of having their immunization records entered into the state vaccine registry. Will these vaccines still be free? The federal Vaccines for Children program continues to cover the recommended schedule at no cost for eligible children, including uninsured children and those on Medicaid, at participating providers and county health departments. How can Florida parents comment on the rule? The health department accepts public input during the 21-day window that opened after the Surgeon General's approval. Details are posted through the department's rulemaking notices. 葛兰素史克 慢性乙型肝炎 药物 Hibsago 获得全球首个批准 - 雅虎财经

GSK Obtains First Global Approval for Chronic Hepatitis B Drug Hibsago - Yahoo Finance UK
新闻简报葛兰素史克(GSK)的药物 Hibsago(bepirovirsen)作为 功能性治愈 获得全球首个批准,用于治疗 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒感染的成年患者。该批准由日本厚生劳动省批准,专门针对已接受至少六个月核苷(酸)类似物治疗并符合预先定义的病毒标志物的患者。该决定得到了 3 期 B 井试验数据的支持,该药物在批准前获得了 SENKU 快速通道指定。这标志着 慢性乙型肝炎 治疗的重大进步,因为在 治疗 六个月后,患者有可能摆脱终身治疗并降低长期肝脏并发症的风险。GSK 还在包括美国在内的其他国家推进 Hibsago 的监管申请,预计将在未来几个月内做出决定。消息公布后,该公司股价在早盘交易中小幅下跌。此次批准是葛兰素史克肝病学产品组合的一个重要里程碑,解决了日本未得到满足的医疗需求。
查看新闻五要素
时间
根据周一提交的文件,日本厚生劳动省批准该药物为 功能性治愈,用于治疗 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒感染的成年患者。该批准专门针对接受至少六个月核苷(酸)类似物治疗并符合预先定义的病毒标志物的患者。葛兰素史克表示,正在其他司法管辖区推进贝匹罗韦森的监管申请,预计未来几个月在包括美国在内的地区做出决定。
地点与对象
日本,该药被批准用于治疗 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒感染的成年患者。这家总部位于英国的制药集团使用 3 期 B 井试验的数据来支持 Hibsago 在日本的申请。
事件
葛兰素史克 (GSK) 首次获得全球批准 Hibsago 或 bepirovirsen 作为 功能性治愈 用于治疗 慢性乙型肝炎 病毒感染的成年患者。
规模、影响与风险
此次批准是 慢性乙型肝炎 管理层的重大进步。经过 6 个月的 治疗 与 Hibsago 治疗后,患者可以摆脱终身治疗,并降低长期肝脏并发症的风险。该申请基于 2 期 Azur-1 试验的结果,该试验显示很大一部分参与者在 治疗 一年或更长时间后没有检测到癌症迹象。
应对、状态与不确定性
葛兰素史克股价在早盘交易中小幅下跌。该批准基于 3 期 B-well 试验和 2 期 Azur-1 试验的数据。

GSK Obtains First Global Approval for Chronic Hepatitis B Drug Hibsago - Yahoo Finance UK

News Brief
GSK has obtained the first global approval for its drug Hibsago (bepirovirsen) as a functional cure for adult patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection. The approval, granted by Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, is specific for patients who have undergone at least six months of nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy and meet pre-defined viral markers. The decision was supported by data from the phase 3 B-well trials, where the drug received a SENKU fast-track designation prior to approval. This marks a significant advancement in the management of chronic hepatitis B, as patients could potentially be freed from lifelong therapy and reduce their risk of long-term liver complications after six months of treatment. GSK is also advancing regulatory submissions for Hibsago in other countries, including the US, with decisions expected in the coming months. The company's shares declined marginally in early morning trading following the announcement. The approval is a major milestone in GSK's hepatology portfolio, addressing high unmet medical need in Japan.
Original source text (English)
MT Newswires -Shutterstock GSK (GSK.L) secured the first global approval for Hibsago, or bepirovirsen, after Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare cleared the drug as a functional cure for adult patients with chronic hepatitis B virus infection. The approval is specific for the administration of the antisense oligonucleotide in patients who underwent at least six months of nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy and meet pre-defined viral markers, according to a Monday filing. The UK-based pharmaceutical group used data from the phase 3 B-well trials to support the application for Hibsago in Japan, where the drug had also received a SENKU fast-track designation prior to approval in recognition of its potential to address high unmet medical need. "For the first time, a treatment approved for functional cure is available to people living with chronic hepatitis B in Japan with Hibsago. After 6-months of treatment with Hibsago, patients could be freed from life-long therapy and reduce their risk of long-term liver complications. This is a major advance for CHB management and our innovative hepatology portfolio, and we look forward to further regulatory decisions in other countries," said Chief Scientific Officer Tony Wood. GSK said it is advancing regulatory submissions for bepirovirsen in other jurisdictions, with decisions expected in the coming months in geographies including the US. In another project, GSK also flagged the US Food and Drug Administration's acceptance for priority review of its supplemental biologics license application for Jemperli, or dostarlimab, as a treatment for previously untreated stage II and III mismatch repair deficient locally advanced rectal cancer. The application is based on results from the phase 2 Azur-1 trial, which showed a significant proportion of participants having no detectable signs of cancer one year or more after treatment. GSK shares declined marginally in early morning trading

Florida wants to repeal required school vaccines for chicken pox, Hepatitis B and more - Orlando Weekly
新闻简报佛罗里达州卫生部提议从 PreK-12 学生的入学要求中删除四种 疫苗——乙型肝炎、水痘(水痘)、b 型流感嗜血杆菌 (Hib) 和肺炎球菌结合物。这项政策变更于 2026 年 8 月 20 日获得卫生局局长约瑟夫·拉达波 (Joseph Ladapo) 的批准,是扩大豁免和减少 疫苗 授权的更广泛努力的一部分,该计划已经讨论了近一年。该提案包括扩大宗教豁免范围,将道德和伦理信仰纳入其中,并允许家长和大学生选择不将其 疫苗接种 记录纳入国家数据库。虽然这一举措得到了州长罗恩·德桑蒂斯和其他人的支持,但它遭到了美国儿科学会苏珊·克雷斯利博士等医学专业人士的批评,她警告说,这可能会增加儿童患病的风险。该规则目前正在接受公众审查,最终批准前有 21 天的评论期。证据中没有报告与这些 疫苗 相关的确诊病例、死亡或暴露情况,对公共健康的影响仍不确定。

2026 年 8 月 24 日;该拟议规则于 2026 年 8 月 20 日获得卫生局局长约瑟夫·拉达波 (Joseph Ladapo) 的批准,并有 21 天的公众意见期。
地点与对象
佛罗里达州,美国;公立和私立 PreK-12 学校;学生的家长和监护人。
事件
佛罗里达州卫生部提出了一项规则,将乙型肝炎、水痘(水痘)、b 型流感嗜血杆菌 (Hib) 和肺炎球菌结合物 疫苗 从学校入学要求中删除。这是一项政策建议,而不是已确认的 暴发 或事件。
规模、影响与风险
拟议的变更影响四个 疫苗,它们是机构规则的一部分,而不是州法律的一部分。此举受到医疗专业人士的批评,因为可能会增加儿童的疾病风险,但证据中尚未报告确诊病例、死亡或暴露情况。
应对、状态与不确定性
拟议规则正在接受审查,最终批准前有 21 天的公众意见期。佛罗里达州卫生部尚未回应置评请求。该政策的框架是扩大父母权利和医疗自由的提议,但其对公共健康的影响仍不确定。

Florida wants to repeal required school vaccines for chicken pox, Hepatitis B and more - Orlando Weekly

News Brief
The Florida Department of Health is proposing to remove four vaccines—Hepatitis B, varicella (chicken pox), Haemophilus influenza type b (Hib), and pneumococcal conjugate—from school entry requirements for PreK-12 students. This policy change, approved by Surgeon General Joseph Ladapo on August 20, 2026, is part of a broader effort to expand exemptions and reduce vaccine mandates, which has been in discussion for nearly a year. The proposal includes expanding religious exemptions to include moral and ethical beliefs and allowing parents and college students to opt out of having their vaccination records included in the state database. While the move has been supported by Governor Ron DeSantis and others, it has faced criticism from medical professionals like Dr. Susan Kressly of the American Academy of Pediatrics, who warned that it could increase disease risk among children. The rule is currently under public review with a 21-day comment period before final approval. No confirmed cases, deaths, or exposures related to these vaccines are reported in the evidence, and the impact on public health remains uncertain.

The Florida Department of Health is proposing a rule to remove Hepatitis B, varicella (chicken pox), Haemophilus influenza type b (Hib) and pneumococcal conjugate vaccines for public school attendance, a move that has been in play for almost a year after Surgeon General Joseph Ladapo announced his intent to get rid of all vaccine mandates in the state. The rule, which was approved by Ladapo on Aug. 20, has a 21-day period for public input before final approval. DOH did not immediately respond to a request for comment Monday. The proposed rule also expands religious vaccine exemptions to include moral and ethical beliefs and lets parents and college students opt out of having their records included in the state vaccine database. Florida currently allows religious exemptions “if immunizations are in conflict with the religious tenets and practices of the child’s parent or guardian,” according to DOH. Without an exemption, Florida law requires students to receive vaccinations for measles, mumps and rubella (MMR), polio, diphtheria, rubeola and tetanus to attend K-12 public schools. But the immunizations considered for repeal by DOH are only an agency rule, not in state law, and can be repealed by the agency itself. Last September, Gov. Ron DeSantis and Ladapo called on the Legislature to roll back all vaccine mandates in the state. “Every last one of them is wrong and drips with disdain and slavery,” Ladapo said in Valrico, Hillsborough County, at the time. “Who am I to tell you what your child should put in their body? I don’t have that right. Your body is a gift from God,” he added. In response, American Academy of Pediatrics President Dr. Susan Kressly said the move will put children at risk of getting sick. “The AAP believes every family should have access to immunizations to keep their community healthy,” Kressly said in a released statement. “Schools are an important part of that community. For many kids, the best part of school is being with friends — sharing space, playing on the playground and trading germs. Close contact makes it easy for contagious diseases to spread quickly.” Even though the move to repeal all vaccine mandates was supported by DeSantis, First Lady Casey DeSantis and then-Education Commissioner Anastasios Kamoutsas, no legislator filed a bill in any of the multiple legislative sessions in 2026 to remove those requirements from Florida law. Multiple attempts at a “Medical Freedom” bill that would have expanded vaccine exemptions and mandated doctors to provide an alternate vaccine schedule passed the state Senate but failed to pass the state House. In December 2025, DOH held an open meeting in Panama City to discuss changing the vaccination requirements for public schools, which Emma Spencer, a director within DOH, said was “grounded in policy based on considerations that favor parental rights and medical freedom.” Parents’ rights advocates praised the state and also repeated false claims, such as vaccines cause autism, while doctors from around the state pleaded with DOH to reconsider and said it would turn back the clock on medical advancements. Eehab Kenawy, a Panama City pediatrician, said religious exemptions already exist to allow parents and guardians to opt out of vaccinations for their children. “You’re not forced. But sending a message to the general public that vaccines are not important, vaccines are not needed, is not the way to do it,” Kenawy said. AusperBio Completes $120 Million Series C Financing to Advance AHB-137 Toward Potential Commercialization and Expand Next-Generation HBV Therapies - PR Newswire

AusperBio Completes $120 Million Series C Financing to Advance AHB-137 Toward Potential Commercialization and Expand Next-Generation HBV Therapies - PR Newswire
新闻简报AusperBio has completed a $120 million Series C financing to advance AHB-137 toward potential commercialization and expand next-generation hepatitis B virus (HBV) therapies. AHB-137 is currently being evaluated in a Phase 3 trial in China for the functional cure of chronic hepatitis B (CHB), following a global Phase 1 study and multiple Phase 2 studies. Chris Yang, co-founder and CSO of AusperBio, stated that AHB-137 has demonstrated promising clinical activity in patients. The trial is ongoing, and no specific case counts, death counts, or exposure numbers are reported in the supplied evidence. The progress of AHB-137 is under investigation, with results yet to be confirmed. This development is part of broader efforts to address HBV infection, particularly chronic hepatitis B, which remains a significant public health challenge globally.

Inquiries Editorial Bureaus Partnerships Media Inquiries Worldwide Offices Hamburger menu Send a Release ALL CONTACT INFO Contact Us 888-776-0942 from 8 AM - 10 PM ET AusperBio Completes $120 Million Series C Financing to Advance AHB-137 Toward Potential Commercialization and Expand Next-Generation HBV Therapies News provided by AusperBio Therapeutics Inc. Aug 27, 2026, 20:00 ET Share this article Share toX Share this article Share toX Financing supports advancement of AHB-137 toward potential commercialization, including its Phase 3 registrational program and commercialization readiness Proceeds will also accelerate AHB-171 and next-generation combination approaches designed to advance functional cure for chronic hepatitis B Series C brings AusperBio's total capital raised to $360 million since 2024 SAN FRANCISCO, Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AusperBio Therapeutics, Inc. and Ausper Biopharma Co., Ltd. (collectively "AusperBio" or the "Company"), a near-commercial biopharmaceutical company focused on developing targeted oligonucleotide therapeutics for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and other diseases, today announced the closing of its $120 million Series C financing. The financing was led by a leading strategic investor, with participation from new investor RA Capital Management, L.P. ("RA Capital"), alongside continued support from AusperBio's existing investors, including HanKang Capital, Sherpa Capital, InnoPinnacle Fund, Qiming Venture Partners, YuanBio Venture Capital, and CDH Investments. With the completion of the Series C, AusperBio has raised $360 million since 2024, reflecting strong and sustained investor confidence in the potential of the Company's lead programs and differentiated oligonucleotide platforms. The financing will support the continued development of AHB-137, AusperBio's lead investigational ASO therapy for CHB, including its Phase 3 registrational program and commercialization readiness. Proceeds will also accelerate the development of AHB-171, the Company's investigational HBV siRNA candidate built on its proprietary Au-HALOTM targeted delivery platform, advance next-generation combination approaches for CHB, and further expand the Company's pipeline of targeted oligonucleotide therapeutics addressing significant unmet medical needs. "This financing represents an important inflection point for AusperBio as we advance AHB-137 toward potential commercialization while developing next-generation therapies for CHB," said Dr. Guofeng Cheng, co-founder and CEO of AusperBio. "We are grateful for the continued confidence of our existing investors and pleased to welcome RA Capital to AusperBio. We look forward to building on this momentum to advance our strategy toward functional cure and unlock new opportunities across our oligonucleotide platforms." Dr. Chris Yang, co-founder and CSO of AusperBio, added, "AHB-137 has demonstrated promising clinical activity in patients and has the potential to serve as a backbone therapy for functional cure of CHB. Our Med-OligoTM ASO, Au-HALOTM targeted delivery and siRNA discovery platforms enable complementary approaches designed to achieve deeper and more durable antiviral responses. This financing will enable us to further advance these platforms and build on their potential to generate differentiated targeted oligonucleotide therapies for CHB and other diseases with significant unmet medical needs." About AHB-137 AHB-137 is AusperBio's lead investigational unconjugated antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB), developed using the Company's proprietary Med-OligoTM ASO platform. AHB-137 is designed to suppress hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) production, inhibit viral DNA replication, and promote immune reactivation, with the goal of achieving a functional cure for CHB. AHB-137 has demonstrated promising clinical results and is currently being evaluated in a Phase 3 trial in China, following completion of a global Phase 1 study and multiple Phase 2 studies. The Company is advancing AHB-137 through a coordinated global development strategy toward potential commercialization. AHB-137 is an investigational product candidate and has not been approved by any regulatory authority. About AHB-171 AHB-171 is an investigational hepatocyte-targeted siRNA therapeutic candidate for the treatment of CHB that leverages AusperBio's proprietary Au-HALOTM liver-targeting delivery platform. AHB-171 is designed to selectively suppress viral gene expression and provide potent and sustained antiviral activity. As the first clinical candidate developed using the Au-HALOTM platform, AHB-171 is advancing the clinical validation of the Company's targeted delivery and siRNA capabilities and broadening the Company's differentiated HBV pipeline. AHB-171 is an investigational product candidate and has not been approved by any regulatory authority. About Chronic Hepatitis B Chronic hepatitis B remains a significant global health burden, affecting an estimated 254 million people worldwide and causing approximately 1.1 million deaths annually, primarily from cirrhosis and liver cancer, according to the World Health Organization. Current therapies can suppress viral replication but rarely achieve a functional cure, leaving many patients requiring long-term treatment. About AusperBio AusperBio is a near-commercial biopharmaceutical company focused on developing differentiated oligonucleotide therapeutics and targeted delivery technologies, with an initial focus on achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B. The Company's innovation engine is built on its proprietary Med-OligoTM ASO and Au-HALOTM targeted delivery platforms, supporting the development of therapies across multiple oligonucleotide modalities. With multiple clinical-stage programs and a growing pipeline, AusperBio is advancing a backbone-based combination strategy for functional cure of CHB while exploring opportunities in additional disease areas with significant unmet medical needs. 【期刊导读】超80%的MAFLD合并CHB患者存在显著肝脏炎症,肥胖加剧炎症负荷-MedSci.cn - 梅斯医学 MedSci

News article (Chinese original; verified English title unavailable)
新闻简报厦门大学中医院和解放军总医院第五医学中心的研究人员在PeerJ上发表的一项研究表明,80.8%的代谢相关性脂肪肝病(MAFLD)和慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)患者存在明显的肝脏炎症(G≥2)。这项针对 447 名新治疗患者进行的研究发现,BMI 与肝脏炎症严重程度呈显着正相关,肥胖患者的严重炎症 发病率 明显较高(93.3%)。BMI、肝脏硬度测量(LSM)、丙氨酸转氨酶(ALT)和 HBV DNA 被确定为严重肝脏炎症的独立危险因素。该研究强调了将体重管理、血糖和血脂控制纳入这些患者综合 治疗 策略的重要性,同时开发用于肝脏炎症风险分层的非侵入性工具,以指导个体化 治疗 决策并改善长期结果。

Original title (Chinese)
【期刊导读】超80%的MAFLD合并CHB患者存在显著肝脏炎症,肥胖加剧炎症负荷-MedSci.cn - 梅斯医学 MedSci
News Brief
A study published in PeerJ by researchers from Xiamen University Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine and the Fifth Medical Center of the PLA General Hospital reveals that 80.8% of patients with metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) and chronic hepatitis B (CHB) have significant liver inflammation (G ≥ 2). The research, conducted on 447 newly treated patients, found that BMI is significantly positively correlated with liver inflammation severity, with obese patients showing a notably higher incidence of severe inflammation (93.3%). BMI, liver stiffness measurement (LSM), alanine aminotransferase (ALT), and HBV DNA were identified as independent risk factors for significant liver inflammation. The study highlights the importance of integrating weight management, glucose, and lipid control into comprehensive treatment strategies for these patients, alongside the development of non-invasive tools for liver inflammation risk stratification to guide individualized treatment decisions and improve long-term outcomes.

Kendall’s tau‐b = 0.091, P = 0.035)。 图1:MAFLD合并CHB患者的肝脏炎症分级分布 注:Group1为正常体重组、Group2为超重组、Group3为肥胖组 正常体重组的显著肝脏炎症(G ≥ 2)比例为77.3%、超重组为80.7%、肥胖组为93.3%,呈递增趋势。肥胖组的重度炎症(G4)占比为8.9%,显著高于正常体重组(1.2%)和超重组(0.4%)。 图2:MAFLD合并CHB患者中显著肝脏炎症(G ≥ 2)的占比 02 BMI、LSM、ALT及HBV DNA是显著肝脏炎症的独立影响因素 单因素分析显示,显著肝脏炎症(G ≥ 2)与BMI、LSM、PLT、ALT、AST、GGT、HDL、HBV DNA、HBeAg阳性及AAGP相关。校正混杂因素后,多因素Logistic回归模型表明BMI(OR = 1.12, 95% CI: 1.01 ‐ 1.26, P = 0.040)、LSM(OR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.17 ‐ 1.53, P < 0.001)、ALT(OR = 1.01, 95% CI: 1.01 ‐ 1.02, P = 0.005)、HBV DNA(OR = 1.32, 95% CI: 1.16 ‐ 1.51, P < 0.001)是显著肝脏炎症(G ≥ 2)的独立影响因素。 表3:MAFLD合并CHB患者发生显著肝脏炎症的独立影响因素 肝霖君有话说 MAFLD与CHB共存增加了肝脏炎症评估及临床决策的复杂性。本研究基于肝活检数据,在447例MAFLD合并CHB初治患者中发现,80.8%的患者存在显著肝脏炎症,且BMI与肝脏炎症分级呈显著正相关,肥胖患者的显著肝脏炎症发生率高达93.3%。多因素分析进一步证实,BMI、LSM、HBV DNA及ALT是显著肝脏炎症的独立影响因素。 对于MAFLD合并CHB患者,临床管理应兼顾病毒学控制与代谢危险因素干预。在规范抗病毒治疗的基础上,将体重管理、血糖及血脂调控纳入综合治疗方案,协同改善肝脏炎症状态。同时,建立基于无创指标的肝脏炎症风险分层工具,有助于指导个体化治疗决策,改善患者长期预后。 参考文献: Xu LH, He RY, Kang YN, et al. Retrospective analysis of predictors for significant hepatic inflammation in metabolic-associated fatty liver disease with chronic hepatitis B [J]. NA 经治 HBsAg<100 IU/mL 慢乙肝患者,各指南停药标准尚无共识。亚洲人群单纯停药 HBsAg 清除率有限,复发风险高;聚乙二醇干扰素 α 有限疗程方案可显著提升临床治愈率,为优选策略。 临床研究|肝脂肪变性对慢性乙型肝炎病毒载量及肝纤维化进展的影响 本研究采用横断面真实世界研究设计,对大规模CHB临床人群进行系统分析,旨在阐明肝脂肪变性程度与HBV病毒载量及肝纤维化分层之间的关系,以期为CHB合并MASLD患者的风险分层与个体化管理提供循证依据。 当“随意”遇上“盲目”:慢乙肝患者自行停药的一场危机 本文报道一例患者于停药半年后服用减肥产品,短期内发生严重肝损伤并迅速演变为肝衰竭,现将诊疗过程中的若干体会总结如下,以资同道参考。 抗病毒+抗肝纤维化联合治疗策略在LLV管理中的临床价值 系统梳理了LLV的临床现状以及远期风险,探讨了“双抗治疗”在这类人群中的应用价值,为CHB患者长期全程管理提供新思路。肝胆相照平台特将内容整理成文,以飨读者。 【临床治愈集结号】免疫耐受期患者基于Peg-IFNα-2b间歇治疗,先获HBsAg血清学转换再获HBeAg清除,最终实现临床治愈 本期给大家介绍一例有肝癌家族史的免疫耐受期慢性HBV感染者,采用基于聚乙二醇干扰素α-2b间歇治疗策略,在HBsAg清除后HBeAg仍阳性时继续治疗,最终实现临床治愈、安全停药的病例。 临床研究|PEG-IFN-α-2b治疗低水平HBsAg慢性乙型肝炎实现临床治愈的列线图模型 本研究聚焦于HBsAg<1 500 IU/mL的优势患者,分析经PEG-IFN-α-2b治疗48周后实现临床治愈的预测因素,并构建联合预测的列线图模型。 扶正抑癌:中医药降低慢性病毒性肝病肝癌风险的临床策略与机制 本文以深圳三院的“正肝抑癌方”为核心,系统阐述中医“扶正抑癌”策略降低慢性病毒性肝病肝癌风险的理论基础、临床实践与作用机制,为中西医结合防治肝癌提供参考。 梅斯医学 App 前往APP阅读全文,体验更佳 扫描二维码下载梅斯医学APP,参与讨论! 梅斯医学MedSci APP 医路相伴,成就大医 打开 x 科室 肿瘤科 神经科 心血管 呼吸科 消化科 风湿免疫 皮肤科 血液科 骨科 内分泌 订阅+ 更多科室 心血管 肿瘤 内分泌 普通内科 消化 呼吸 神经科 传染科 精神心理 肾内科 风湿免疫 血液科 老年医学 头颈外科 胃肠外科 血管外科 肝胆胰外 骨科 普通外科 胸心外科 神经外科 泌尿外科 烧伤科 整形美容 麻醉疼痛 罕见病 医学科研 康复医学 核医学/放疗 营养科 药械 儿科 耳鼻咽喉 口腔科 眼科 政策人文 全科医学 预防公卫 妇产科 中医科 急重症 皮肤性病 影像放射 转化医学 检验病理 护理 糖尿病 冠心病 肝病 乳腺癌 职业安全 患者招募 药物经济 人工智能 细胞基因治疗 医生集团 医学科普 临床研究 知识产权 医学教育 研究设计 智慧医疗 中国学者 公司产业 工具 期刊查询 临床指南 医学计算 基金查询 精品课 学术直播 公开课 循证助手 医讯达 全部工具 服务 科研数智化 真实世界研究解决方案 数字化学术传播解决方案 其它

GSK's Hibsago wins first global approval in Japan as functional cure for chronic hep B - The Pharma Letter

News Brief
GSK's Hibsago (bepirovirsen) has received its first global approval in Japan for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) as a functional cure. The approval was announced on Monday, 28 August 2026, by GSK and confirmed by Japan's Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare. It is the first regulatory clearance for bepirovirsen worldwide and the first functional cure treatment for CHB approved in Japan. The treatment is intended for adults who have received at least six months of prior nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy and meet specified viral marker thresholds. The article is accessible to registered users, but no further details on the approval process or risk assessment were provided. This development represents a significant milestone in the treatment of chronic hepatitis B, offering a new therapeutic option for patients in Japan and potentially other regions.

学术前沿|Hepatology:有限疗程序贯方案对乙肝功能性治愈有益-MedSci.cn - 梅斯医学 MedSci

News article (Chinese original; verified English title unavailable)
新闻简报2026 年 8 月 4 日《肝病学》在线发表的一项多中心随机试验报告称,在接受至少三年核苷(酸)类似物治疗的非肝硬化、HBeAg 阴性 慢性乙型肝炎 患者中,停止 NA,然后在 4 周后添加为期 16 周的聚乙二醇干扰素疗程,与单独停止 NA 相比,3 年 HBsAg 血清清除率增加了四倍多(14.3% 对比 3.0%)。干扰素组停药后严重肝炎发作的风险也降低了一半(13.4% vs 27.9%)。各组之间的 Re-治疗 率相似。作者警告说,该试验未达到其招募目标,基因型分析是探索性的,该方案应保留给精心挑选的患者,密切监测病情发作,并在有指征时立即恢复 抗病毒药物 治疗。
查看新闻五要素
时间
发表时间:2026-08-27;研究事件日期:2026-08-04。
地点与对象
全球多中心试验;主要站点英国伦敦帝国理工学院;研究人群:接受核苷(酸)类似物(NA)治疗≥3年的非肝硬化、HBeAg阴性慢性乙型肝炎患者。
事件
一项多中心随机对照试验 (NUC-B) 报道,在 慢性乙型肝炎 患者中,在 NA 撤药 4 周后开始为期 16 周的聚乙二醇化干扰素 (PEG-IFN) 疗程,与单独撤药 NA 相比,显着提高了 3 年 HBsAg 血清清除率。
规模、影响与风险
入组 156 名患者(1:1 随机分组);使用 PEG-IFN 的 3 年 HBsAg 血清清除率为 14.3%,而未使用 PEG-IFN 时为 3.0%(p=0.037;HR 5.68,p=0.025)。使用 PEG-IFN 的严重肝炎发作累积 发病率 为 13.4%,而没有使用 PEG-IFN 则为 27.9%(OR 0.38,p=0.028)。NA re-治疗 率没有统计学差异(28.4% vs 34.9%,p=0.13)。
应对、状态与不确定性
试验未达到计划样本量;基因型分层分析是探索性的,效力有限;结果仅适用于非肝硬化患者;建议严格选择患者,密切监测肝功能和 HBV DNA,并在出现耀斑时及时重新启动 NA。

Original title (Chinese)
学术前沿|Hepatology:有限疗程序贯方案对乙肝功能性治愈有益-MedSci.cn - 梅斯医学 MedSci
News Brief
A multi-center randomized trial published online in Hepatology on 4 August 2026 reports that, among non-cirrhotic, HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients who had received at least three years of nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy, stopping NA and then adding a 16-week course of pegylated interferon four weeks later more than quadrupled the 3-year HBsAg seroclearance rate compared with stopping NA alone (14.3% vs 3.0%). The interferon group also halved the risk of severe hepatitis flares after withdrawal (13.4% vs 27.9%). Re-treatment rates were similar between groups. The authors caution that the trial fell short of its recruitment target, genotype analyses were exploratory, and the regimen should be reserved for carefully selected patients with close monitoring for flares and prompt resumption of antiviral therapy when indicated.

临床肝胆病杂志 临床肝胆病杂志 发表于上海 慢性乙型肝炎 临床肝胆病杂志 / 关注 互相关注 NUC‐B 试验显示,长期 NA 抑制的非肝硬化 HBeAg 阴性慢乙肝患者,NA 停药后序贯 16 周短程 PEG‐IFN,可提升 3 年 HBsAg 清除率并减少重度肝炎发作。 深度解析医学证据,DeepEvidence为你支撑决策 慢性乙型肝炎全球感染基数庞大,疾病进展可发展为肝硬化、肝细胞癌,带来沉重的社会医疗负担。目前核苷(酸)类似物是慢性乙肝的一线治疗药物,能够有效抑制乙肝病毒复制,减少终末期肝病的发生,但该类药物难以清除肝细胞内的病毒共价闭合环状 DNA,绝大多数患者需要长期维持用药,很难达到临床追求的功能性治愈,也就是乙肝表面抗原的持续转阴。聚乙二醇干扰素(PEG-IFN)可调节机体抗病毒免疫,能够实现部分患者 HBsAg 清除,但传统疗程长、不良反应较多,一定程度上限制临床使用。现有指南提出,经核苷类似物长期治疗后的 HBeAg 阴性慢乙肝患者,可以考虑尝试停药。停药后部分患者依靠自身免疫能够实现表面抗原清除,但总体转阴比例偏低,而且停药后还可能出现肝炎急性加重,严重者会发生肝脏失代偿,因此该方案的临床使用十分谨慎。已有研究提示,核苷类似物停药后人体抗病毒免疫会出现一过性激活。基于这一现象,本研究设想,在停药后免疫应答活跃的窗口期,加用短疗程聚乙二醇干扰素,进一步调动机体免疫能力,以此提高功能性治愈的概率,同时评估该联合方案的安全性,由此开展 NUCB 这项多中心随机对照临床试验。 2026年8月4日,伦敦帝国理工学院Mark Thursz团队于Hepatology在线发表一项多中心随机对照 NUC-B 试验。研究纳入非肝硬化、HBeAg 阴性、NA 治疗不少于 3 年的慢性乙型肝炎患者。计划入组 240 例,受疫情及患者干扰素接受度影响,最终 1:1 随机纳入 156 例受试者。受试者分为两组,对照组直接停用 NA;干预组停用 NA,间隔 4 周后给予 16 周短程聚乙二醇干扰素治疗,开展为期 3 年随访。主要终点为 3 年 HBsAg 清除率,次要终点包括 qHBsAg 动态变化、NA 重启治疗率、重度肝炎发作等安全性指标。结果显示:3 年随访 HBsAg 清除率,对照组仅 3.0%,干扰素干预组可达 14.3%(p=0.037);KM 曲线提示干扰素组实现 HBsAg 清除的风险显著升高(HR=5.68,p=0.025),全程随访干扰素组 qHBsAg 下降幅度显著优于对照组。安全性方面十分值得关注:对照组重度肝炎发作累积发生率 27.9%,干扰素组仅 13.4%(OR=0.38,p=0.028),加用短程 PEG-IFN 可显著降低停药后重度肝炎发作;发生重度肝炎发作的患者无一例获得 HBsAg 清除。而需要重启 NA 治疗比例两组无统计学差异(28.4% vs 34.9%,p=0.13)。基因型探索分析提示 A 型患者 qHBsAg 下降趋势更显著,但样本量有限,仅为探索性结果。 NA 停药 ± 短程 PEG-IFN 组 3 年 HBsAg 清除及表面抗原定量变化 该 NUC-B 随机对照研究证实,对于非肝硬化、经长期 NA 抑制的 HBeAg 阴性慢乙肝患者,NA 停药后间隔 4 周序贯 16 周短程 PEG-IFN,相较于单纯停药,可显著提升 3 年 HBsAg 功能性清除率,同时降低停药后重度肝炎发作风险,为有限疗程追求慢乙肝临床治愈提供全新思路。 但本研究未达到预设样本量,基因型分层分析样本偏少,研究对象仅限非肝硬化人群,结论不可外推至肝硬化患者。临床实践中若考虑采用该方案,需严格筛选适用人群,充分与受试者沟通获益及潜在风险;停药阶段严密监测肝功能、HBV DNA,及时处置肝炎发作,必要时重启 NA 抗病毒治疗。 View five news elements
Time
Published 2026-08-27; study event date 2026-08-04.
Location and population
Global multi-center trial; lead site Imperial College London, United Kingdom; study population: non-cirrhotic, HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B patients with ≥3 years of nucleos(t)ide analogue (NA) therapy.
Event
A multi-center randomized controlled trial (NUC-B) reported that a limited 16-week pegylated interferon (PEG-IFN) course, started 4 weeks after NA withdrawal, significantly increased 3-year HBsAg seroclearance versus NA withdrawal alone in chronic hepatitis B patients.
Scale, impact and risk
Enrolled 156 patients (1:1 randomization); 3-year HBsAg seroclearance 14.3% with PEG-IFN vs 3.0% without (p=0.037; HR 5.68, p=0.025). Severe hepatitis flare cumulative incidence 13.4% with PEG-IFN vs 27.9% without (OR 0.38, p=0.028). No statistical difference in NA re-treatment rates (28.4% vs 34.9%, p=0.13).
Response, status and uncertainty
Trial did not reach planned sample size; genotype-stratified analyses were exploratory with limited power; results apply only to non-cirrhotic patients; strict patient selection, close monitoring of liver function and HBV DNA, and timely NA re-initiation are advised if flares occur.

Europe set to miss 2030 hepatitis elimination targets, health agency warns - AOL.ca
新闻简报The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) warns that Europe is off track to meet its 2030 hepatitis elimination targets. Despite progress in preventing hepatitis B and C, an estimated five million people in the region still live with chronic infections, and around 60,000 die annually from liver disease linked to these infections. The proportion of acute hepatitis B cases among those under 25 years old has decreased from 11% in 2015 to 8% in 2024, reflecting the impact of childhood vaccination programs. However, only a minority of countries have achieved the World Health Organization (WHO) target of fully vaccinating 95% of children against hepatitis B, and coverage of harm reduction measures remains inadequate. The ECDC highlights the need for improved access to interventions and systematic monitoring to address these gaps and ensure the elimination targets are met.

地点与对象
该报告重点关注欧盟和欧洲经济区(包括所有 30 个成员国),并强调了这对数百万欧洲人,特别是 25 岁以下的欧洲人的影响。
事件
ECDC 报告称,尽管在预防乙型肝炎和丙型肝炎方面取得了进展,但该地区尚未步入实现 2030 年消除目标的轨道,数百万人仍然患有慢性感染,而且许多人不知道自己的状况。
规模、影响与风险
An estimated five million people in Europe are living with chronic hepatitis B or C, and around 60,000 die annually from liver disease linked to these infections. The proportion of acute hepatitis B cases among people under 25 fell from 11% in 2015 to 8% in 2024, but gaps remain in vaccination coverage.
应对、状态与不确定性
ECDC 指出,有效的预防和 治疗 解决方案是可用的,但儿童常规 疫苗接种 方面的差距以及减少伤害措施的覆盖范围仍然不足。他们强调需要进行系统监测和改善干预措施的可及性。

Europe set to miss 2030 hepatitis elimination targets, health agency warns - AOL.ca

News Brief
The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) warns that Europe is off track to meet its 2030 hepatitis elimination targets. Despite progress in preventing hepatitis B and C, an estimated five million people in the region still live with chronic infections, and around 60,000 die annually from liver disease linked to these infections. The proportion of acute hepatitis B cases among those under 25 years old has decreased from 11% in 2015 to 8% in 2024, reflecting the impact of childhood vaccination programs. However, only a minority of countries have achieved the World Health Organization (WHO) target of fully vaccinating 95% of children against hepatitis B, and coverage of harm reduction measures remains inadequate. The ECDC highlights the need for improved access to interventions and systematic monitoring to address these gaps and ensure the elimination targets are met.
Original source text (English)
Despite progress over the last few years in preventing hepatitis B and C, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) warns the region is off track to meet the 2030 elimination targets. “No one should die from a disease that is preventable, diagnosable and treatable, yet millions of Europeans are living with chronic hepatitis B or C infections – often without knowing it – which can lead to severe long-term consequences such as liver failure or liver cancer,” said Bruno Ciancio, Head of Unit for Directly Transmitted and Vaccine-Preventable Diseases at ECDC. Hepatitis B and C are transmitted through infected blood or bodily fluids and are among the leading causes of chronic liver disease. While acute hepatitis B infections have been falling steadily since 2006, driven by long-standing vaccination and prevention efforts, an estimated five million people in Europe are still living with chronic hepatitis B or C, and around 60,000 die every year from liver disease linked to these infections, according to the ECDC. Among people younger than 25 years, the proportion of acute hepatitis B cases fell from 11% in 2015 to 8% in 2024, reflecting the impact of childhood vaccination programmes and other prevention measures. Routine screening for hepatitis B in pregnancy is also well established across all 30 European Union and European Economic Area countries, helping to bring down transmission of the virus from mother to child to below 2%, the ECDC said. Ciancio noted that effective control solutions are already in place. Those include vaccination to prevent hepatitis B, harm reduction and infection control initiatives to reduce transmission, testing to identify infections early, and treatments that can cure hepatitis C and control hepatitis B. Millions in Europe unknowingly living with hepatitis, health authorities warn However, experts have identified gaps in routine childhood vaccination. Only a minority of countries have reached the World Health Organization (WHO) target of fully vaccinating 95% of children against hepatitis B, with others even reporting a decline in coverage in recent years. Harm reduction measures — such as opioid agonist treatment and the provision of sterile needles and syringes — are effective in limiting transmission of hepatitis C. Still, coverage remains inadequate, and only seven countries meet the WHO target for distributing sterile injection equipment to people who inject drugs. “Our collective challenge is to ensure that these life-saving interventions are accessible to everyone who needs them,” Ciancio said. Sexual transmission remains a major route of hepatitis B transmission. For hepatitis C, most cases are linked to injecting drug use and sex between men. Yet, the ECDC noted that specific prevention efforts targeting sexual transmission of hepatitis across different populations have not been systematically monitored across countries

Time
The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) warns that Europe is off track to meet the 2030 hepatitis elimination targets, with the report published on 2026-08-26.
Location and population
The report focuses on the European Union and European Economic Area, which includes all 30 member countries, and highlights the impact on millions of Europeans, particularly those younger than 25 years.
Event
The ECDC reports that despite progress in preventing hepatitis B and C, the region is not on track to meet the 2030 elimination targets, with millions still living with chronic infections and many unaware of their status.
Scale, impact and risk
An estimated five million people in Europe are living with chronic hepatitis B or C, and around 60,000 die annually from liver disease linked to these infections. The proportion of acute hepatitis B cases among people under 25 fell from 11% in 2015 to 8% in 2024, but gaps remain in vaccination coverage.
Response, status and uncertainty
The ECDC notes that effective prevention and treatment solutions are available, but gaps in routine childhood vaccination and inadequate coverage of harm reduction measures persist. They emphasize the need for systematic monitoring and improved access to interventions.

Labcorp Launches Hepatitis D Reflex Testing for Earlier Detection - Clinical Lab Products

News Brief
Labcorp has launched hepatitis D reflex testing as part of its efforts to improve early detection of the virus. This new testing method allows for automatic screening of hepatitis D in patients who test positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, addressing the issue of underdiagnosis. The initiative is part of broader advancements in diagnostic technologies, including the development of AI-assisted platforms and other innovative testing methods. While the introduction of this test is a significant step in enhancing diagnostic capabilities, the specific scale of impact or risk associated with hepatitis D remains unclear based on the provided evidence. The testing is currently being implemented, and further details on its effectiveness and outcomes are expected to be released in the coming months.

新闻简报路透社健康新闻摘要重点介绍了与 乙型肝炎病毒 (HBV) 及其相关疗法相关的最新监管进展。2026年8月25日,葛兰素史克宣布其实验性药物慢性乙型肝炎在日本获得全球首个批准,标志着乙肝感染治疗迈出了重要一步。此外,一种关键的癌症疗法作为可能的直肠癌 治疗 获得了美国监管机构的优先审查。然而,证据并未提供这些事态发展的具体病例数、死亡人数或暴露人数。美国食品和药物管理局 (FDA) 还扩大了强生公司药物的批准范围,用于治疗一种罕见的血液疾病,特别是温性自身免疫性溶血性贫血 (wAIHA),适用于 12 岁及以上已经或正在接受类固醇治疗的患者。此次批准使 Imaavy 成为第一个获得这种情况许可的 治疗。证据没有提及任何正在进行的与乙型肝炎相关的调查、测试或隔离措施,也没有提供有关药物或治疗现状的详细信息。该摘要重点关注监管行动,而不是 暴发 细节或公共卫生应对措施。

Reuters Health News Summary - Devdiscourse

News Brief
Reuters Health News Summary highlights recent regulatory developments related to hepatitis B virus (HBV) and its associated therapies. On August 25, 2026, GSK announced that its experimental chronic hepatitis B drug received its first global approval in Japan, marking a significant step in the treatment of HBV infection. Additionally, a key cancer therapy was granted a priority U.S. regulatory review as a possible rectal cancer treatment. However, the evidence does not provide specific case counts, death counts, or exposure numbers for these developments. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) also expanded approval for Johnson & Johnson's drug to treat a rare blood disorder, specifically warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia (wAIHA), for patients aged 12 and older who have been or are currently treated with steroids. This approval makes Imaavy the first treatment cleared for this condition. The evidence does not mention any ongoing investigations, testing, or isolation measures related to HBV, nor does it provide details on the current status of the drug or therapy. The summary focuses on regulatory actions rather than outbreak details or public health responses.

China's rate of overweight or obese people could reach more than 65% by 2030, the country's National Health Commission has said. The test, Elecsys pTau217, is a biomarker blood test that can help doctors identify patients who are likely or unlikely to have Alzheimer's-related brain changes, Roche said on Monday. India wanted red flags on chip packets and soda. Big Food fought back A can of Fanta sold in London has 63 calories. Buy the same brand in India, and it contains three times as much sugar. It also includes artificial dye, whose presence in food products in Europe requires a prominent health warning. In India, the colorant’s presence is noted merely in small print on the back of the can. AusperBio Completes $120 Million Series C Financing to Advance AHB-137 Toward Potential Commercialization and Expand Next-Generation HBV Therapies

AusperBio Completes $120 Million Series C Financing to Advance AHB-137 Toward Potential Commercialization and Expand Next-Generation HBV Therapies
新闻简报AusperBio Therapeutics, Inc. and Ausper Biopharma Co., Ltd. announced the completion of a $120 million Series C financing on August 27, 2026, to advance AHB-137 and AHB-171 toward potential commercialization and expand next-generation therapies for chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The financing supports the Phase 3 registrational program for AHB-137, which is an investigational antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy designed to suppress HBsAg production, inhibit viral DNA replication, and promote immune reactivation. AHB-171, an investigational siRNA therapeutic candidate, leverages the Au-HALOTM liver-targeting delivery platform. Both therapies are in development and have not been approved by any regulatory authority. Chronic hepatitis B affects an estimated 254 million people globally and causes around 1.1 million deaths annually, primarily from cirrhosis and liver cancer. The financing reflects strong investor confidence in AusperBio's differentiated oligonucleotide platforms and its strategy to achieve a functional cure for CHB.

News Brief
AusperBio Therapeutics, Inc. and Ausper Biopharma Co., Ltd. announced the completion of a $120 million Series C financing on August 27, 2026, to advance AHB-137 and AHB-171 toward potential commercialization and expand next-generation therapies for chronic hepatitis B (CHB). The financing supports the Phase 3 registrational program for AHB-137, which is an investigational antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy designed to suppress HBsAg production, inhibit viral DNA replication, and promote immune reactivation. AHB-171, an investigational siRNA therapeutic candidate, leverages the Au-HALOTM liver-targeting delivery platform. Both therapies are in development and have not been approved by any regulatory authority. Chronic hepatitis B affects an estimated 254 million people globally and causes around 1.1 million deaths annually, primarily from cirrhosis and liver cancer. The financing reflects strong investor confidence in AusperBio's differentiated oligonucleotide platforms and its strategy to achieve a functional cure for CHB.

AusperBio Completes $120 Million Series C Financing to Advance AHB-137 Toward Potential Commercialization and Expand Next-Generation HBV Therapies PR Newswire Thu, 27 August 2026 at 8:00 pm GMT-4 5 min read Financing supports advancement of AHB-137 toward potential commercialization, including its Phase 3 registrational program and commercialization readiness Proceeds will also accelerate AHB-171 and next-generation combination approaches designed to advance functional cure for chronic hepatitis B Series C brings AusperBio's total capital raised to $360 million since 2024 SAN FRANCISCO, Aug. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AusperBio Therapeutics, Inc. and Ausper Biopharma Co., Ltd. (collectively "AusperBio" or the "Company"), a near-commercial biopharmaceutical company focused on developing targeted oligonucleotide therapeutics for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) and other diseases, today announced the closing of its $120 million Series C financing. AusperBio The financing was led by a leading strategic investor, with participation from new investor RA Capital Management, L.P. ("RA Capital"), alongside continued support from AusperBio's existing investors, including HanKang Capital, Sherpa Capital, InnoPinnacle Fund, Qiming Venture Partners, YuanBio Venture Capital, and CDH Investments. With the completion of the Series C, AusperBio has raised $360 million since 2024, reflecting strong and sustained investor confidence in the potential of the Company's lead programs and differentiated oligonucleotide platforms. The financing will support the continued development of AHB-137, AusperBio's lead investigational ASO therapy for CHB, including its Phase 3 registrational program and commercialization readiness. Proceeds will also accelerate the development of AHB-171, the Company's investigational HBV siRNA candidate built on its proprietary Au-HALOTM targeted delivery platform, advance next-generation combination approaches for CHB, and further expand the Company's pipeline of targeted oligonucleotide therapeutics addressing significant unmet medical needs. "This financing represents an important inflection point for AusperBio as we advance AHB-137 toward potential commercialization while developing next-generation therapies for CHB," said Dr. Guofeng Cheng, co-founder and CEO of AusperBio. "We are grateful for the continued confidence of our existing investors and pleased to welcome RA Capital to AusperBio. We look forward to building on this momentum to advance our strategy toward functional cure and unlock new opportunities across our oligonucleotide platforms." Dr. Chris Yang, co-founder and CSO of AusperBio, added, "AHB-137 has demonstrated promising clinical activity in patients and has the potential to serve as a backbone therapy for functional cure of CHB. Our Med-OligoTM ASO, Au-HALOTM targeted delivery and siRNA discovery platforms enable complementary approaches designed to achieve deeper and more durable antiviral responses. This financing will enable us to further advance these platforms and build on their potential to generate differentiated targeted oligonucleotide therapies for CHB and other diseases with significant unmet medical needs." Story continues About AHB-137 AHB-137 is AusperBio's lead investigational unconjugated antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) therapy for chronic hepatitis B (CHB), developed using the Company's proprietary Med-OligoTM ASO platform. AHB-137 is designed to suppress hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) production, inhibit viral DNA replication, and promote immune reactivation, with the goal of achieving a functional cure for CHB. AHB-137 has demonstrated promising clinical results and is currently being evaluated in a Phase 3 trial in China, following completion of a global Phase 1 study and multiple Phase 2 studies. The Company is advancing AHB-137 through a coordinated global development strategy toward potential commercialization. AHB-137 is an investigational product candidate and has not been approved by any regulatory authority. About AHB-171 AHB-171 is an investigational hepatocyte-targeted siRNA therapeutic candidate for the treatment of CHB that leverages AusperBio's proprietary Au-HALOTM liver-targeting delivery platform. AHB-171 is designed to selectively suppress viral gene expression and provide potent and sustained antiviral activity. As the first clinical candidate developed using the Au-HALOTM platform, AHB-171 is advancing the clinical validation of the Company's targeted delivery and siRNA capabilities and broadening the Company's differentiated HBV pipeline. AHB-171 is an investigational product candidate and has not been approved by any regulatory authority. About Chronic Hepatitis B Chronic hepatitis B remains a significant global health burden, affecting an estimated 254 million people worldwide and causing approximately 1.1 million deaths annually, primarily from cirrhosis and liver cancer, according to the World Health Organization. Current therapies can suppress viral replication but rarely achieve a functional cure, leaving many patients requiring long-term treatment. About AusperBio AusperBio is a near-commercial biopharmaceutical company focused on developing differentiated oligonucleotide therapeutics and targeted delivery technologies, with an initial focus on achieving a functional cure for chronic hepatitis B. The Company's innovation engine is built on its proprietary Med-OligoTM ASO and Au-HALOTM targeted delivery platforms, supporting the development of therapies across multiple oligonucleotide modalities. With multiple clinical-stage programs and a growing pipeline, AusperBio is advancing a backbone-based combination strategy for functional cure of CHB while exploring opportunities in additional disease areas with significant unmet medical needs. This news report highlights the regulatory status of the drug, which is intended for use in managing chronic hepatitis B infections. 【期刊导读】通往临床治愈路上的“信号灯”:读懂聚乙二醇干扰素α的免疫激活信号-MedSci.cn - 梅斯医学 MedSci

News article (Chinese original; verified English title unavailable)
新闻简报该文章于2026年8月26日发表于MedSci.cn,对慢性乙型肝炎(CHB)的治疗中聚乙二醇化干扰素α(PegIFNα)的作用机制和临床结果进行了深入综述。PegIFNα 因其能够激活 宿主 的免疫系统、逆转免疫功能障碍和 T 细胞耗竭而被强调为实现 CHB 临床治愈的关键药物。然而,这种免疫激活也会导致不良反应,例如流感样症状、注射部位反应、血细胞减少、失眠、甲状腺功能障碍和恶心。这些影响通常是可控和可逆的,但需要仔细监测和干预。文章引用了 2026 年的多项研究和专家指南,包括发布的 2026 年《聚乙二醇化干扰素-α 毒性管理专家意见》,旨在帮助临床医生平衡 PegIFNα 的治疗益处和安全性。该研究结果基于临床数据,并不表明任何 暴发 或公共卫生紧急情况。文章为综述,不报道任何确诊或疑似病毒传播病例或感染事件。
查看新闻五要素
时间
该文章发表于2026年08月26日,部分与事件相关的信息可追溯至2026年08月25日。证据涵盖多项2026年的研究与报告。
地点与对象
本文讨论了包括上海在内的不同地点与 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 患者相关的研究和临床结果,并提到了 HBV 感染患者的一般人群。
事件
本文概述了 慢性乙型肝炎 (CHB) 的 治疗 中聚乙二醇化干扰素 α (PegIFNα) 的机制和临床结果,包括其在免疫激活和不良反应管理中的作用。这是一篇评论文章,而不是已确认的 暴发 或事件。
规模、影响与风险
PegIFNα 治疗 在某些 CHB 患者群体中与约 30% 的临床治愈率相关。不良反应包括流感样症状、注射部位反应、血细胞减少、失眠、甲状腺功能障碍和恶心。这些通常是可管理和可逆的,但可能会影响 治疗 的依从性和安全性。
应对、状态与不确定性
本文综述了使用 PegIFNα 治疗慢性乙型肝炎的临床研究和专家指南,包括不良反应的管理策略。它不报告源材料中任何未解决的信息或限制。

Original title (Chinese)
【期刊导读】通往临床治愈路上的“信号灯”:读懂聚乙二醇干扰素α的免疫激活信号-MedSci.cn - 梅斯医学 MedSci
News Brief
This article, published on August 26, 2026, by MedSci.cn, provides an in-depth review of the mechanisms and clinical outcomes of pegylated interferon alpha (PegIFNα) in the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB). PegIFNα is highlighted as a key drug for achieving clinical cure in CHB due to its ability to activate the host's immune system, reversing immune dysfunction and T-cell exhaustion. However, this immune activation can also lead to adverse effects such as flu-like symptoms, injection site reactions, blood cell reduction, insomnia, thyroid dysfunction, and nausea. These effects are generally manageable and reversible, but require careful monitoring and intervention. The article references several studies and expert guidelines from 2026, including the release of the 2026 'Pegylated Interferon-α Toxicity Management Expert Opinion,' which aims to assist clinicians in balancing the therapeutic benefits and safety of PegIFNα. The findings are based on clinical data and do not indicate any outbreak or public health emergency. The article is a review and does not report any confirmed or suspected cases of viral transmission or infection events.

(2)广泛激活先天性和适应性免疫细胞; (3)普遍增强抗原呈递功能; (4)扰乱免疫调节检查点。 这些变化共同构成了PegIFNα诱导的全身性免疫激活状态,这正是其疗效与不良反应的基础。这种强大的免疫应答对清除感染肝细胞至关重要,也成为影响旁组织功能的主要因素。具体机制如下: PegIFNα诱导的全身性免疫激活:驱动抗病毒疗效与不良反应的免疫级联应答 分子信号通路(图A):PegIFNα结合IFNAR并激活JAK-STAT信号通路,从而诱导干扰素刺激基因(ISG)的转录。该信号级联应答会因细胞类型而异。 先天免疫扩增(图B):在巨噬细胞和树突状细胞中,JAK-STAT激活可诱导细胞因子释放,包括TNF-α、IL-6和IFN-γ。在受控条件下,这些局部细胞因子可增强抗原呈递,促进Th1极化,并招募NK细胞,从而发挥抗病毒作用。当细胞因子在全身过度扩增,可导致流感样症状等不良反应。 适应性免疫重塑(图C):在PegIFNα以及IL-12、IL-6、TNF-α和IFN-γ等细胞因子的驱动下,HBV特异性CD8+ T细胞通过颗粒酶B、穿孔素和IFN-γ清除受感染的肝细胞;Tfh细胞通过IL-21促进HBsAb的产生;Th1细胞增强抗病毒免疫应答;效应B细胞则产生HBsAb。另一方面,自身反应性T细胞和B细胞也可能通过抗-TPO和抗-Tg抗体导致组织损伤。 临床结局(图D):当免疫应答聚焦于受感染的肝细胞时,可实现临床治愈;而当免疫应答发生错误导向时,则可能出现多系统不良反应。 PegIFNα相关的不良反应并非偶发副作用,而是其主要机制——即PegIFNα诱导的全身性免疫激活——直接且可预测的结局。疗效所需的免疫激活与导致不良反应的免疫机理之间存在不可分割的联系。 三 PegIFNα治疗的不良反应管理策略 临床管理以主动监测和及时分级干预为基础。总体目标是维持一个可行的治疗窗口,平衡抗病毒疗效与安全性。在临床管理中需采取双向策略:第一,通过剖析个体易感性进行治疗前风险预测;第二,采用动态的、基于循证的干预措施进行治疗中管理,以维持可行的治疗窗口。需定期监测血常规、生化指标和甲状腺功能,监测频率应根据治疗阶段和患者稳定性进行调整。支持性护理对于缓解症状和提高治疗依从性至关重要。 参考文献: Zhu L, Peng F, Pi D, et al. View five news elements
Time
The article was published on 2026-08-26, with some event-related information dated to 2026-08-25. The evidence spans multiple studies and reports from 2026.
Location and population
The article discusses studies and clinical outcomes related to chronic hepatitis B (CHB) patients in various locations, including Shanghai, and mentions general populations of patients with HBV infection.
Event
The article provides an overview of the mechanisms and clinical outcomes of pegylated interferon alpha (PegIFNα) in the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB), including its role in immune activation and the management of adverse effects. It is a review article and not a confirmed outbreak or event.
Scale, impact and risk
PegIFNα treatment has been associated with a clinical cure rate of approximately 30% in certain CHB patient groups. Adverse reactions include flu-like symptoms, injection site reactions, blood cell reduction, insomnia, thyroid dysfunction, and nausea. These are generally manageable and reversible, but may impact treatment adherence and safety.
Response, status and uncertainty
The article presents a review of clinical studies and expert guidelines on the use of PegIFNα for CHB, including management strategies for adverse effects. It does not report any unresolved information or limitations in the source material.

Why we need vaccines - Inquirer.com
新闻简报费城前卫生专员 Walter Tsou 于 2026 年 8 月 27 日发表的文章讨论了 疫苗 在增强乙型肝炎等疾病免疫力方面的重要性。文章强调,乙型肝炎具有高度传染性,可导致慢性感染、肝衰竭和癌症等严重后果,而这些疾病在出生时服用 疫苗 是可以预防的。这篇文章还提到了唐纳德·特朗普总统的行政命令,将儿童 疫苗 的数量从 17 人减少到 11 人,并指出乙型肝炎是被删除的 疫苗 之一。Tsou 认为,疫苗 对于制造抗感染抗体至关重要,政府必须支持医学研究来开发新的 疫苗 和个性化 免疫应答。该文章强调了仅依靠少数抗体来对抗病毒的风险,并呼吁增加对 疫苗 开发的投资,以预防疾病及其相关的医疗费用。

时间
发布于 2026 年 8 月 27 日上午 10:01
地点与对象
美国,特别是宾夕法尼亚州和费城(N3、N14)。
事件
一篇评论文章讨论了 疫苗 的重要性,特别强调了乙型肝炎 疫苗 在预防肝癌和其他疾病中的作用。文章还提到唐纳德·特朗普总统的行政命令,减少儿童 疫苗(N14、N15、N16、N17、N18、N19、N20)的数量。
规模、影响与风险
文章指出,乙型肝炎是一种传染性很强的病毒,传染性甚至比艾滋病毒还要强,可导致慢性感染、肝功能衰竭和癌症。它强调,这些结果可以通过出生时注射 疫苗 来预防(N16、N17、N18、N19、N20)。
应对、状态与不确定性
该文章讨论了 疫苗 的重要性以及政府在医学研究中支持的必要性,但没有提供与乙型肝炎(N14、N21、N22、N23、N24、N25、N26、N27、N28、N29、N30、N31、N32、N33、N34、N35、 N36、N37、N38、N39、N40、N41、N42、N43、N44)。
B routine priorityPublic-health news

Why we need vaccines - Inquirer.com

News Brief
The article published on August 27, 2026, by Walter Tsou, former health commissioner of Philadelphia, discusses the importance of vaccines in building immunity against diseases like hepatitis B. It highlights that hepatitis B is highly infectious and can lead to severe outcomes such as chronic infection, liver failure, and cancer, which are preventable with a vaccine given at birth. The piece also references President Donald Trump's executive order to reduce the number of childhood vaccines from 17 to 11, noting that hepatitis B is among the vaccines being removed. Tsou argues that vaccines are essential for creating antibodies to fight infections and that the government must support medical research to develop new vaccines and personalized immune responses. The article emphasizes the risks of relying on only a few antibodies to combat viruses and calls for increased investment in vaccine development to prevent diseases and their associated healthcare costs.
